newsitem.title: UK: Barclays chief says UK not ready for EMU - paper.
newsitem.headline: Barclays chief says UK not ready for EMU - paper.

text.p: The chief executive of Barclays Plc Martin Taylor said Britain was not ready to join European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU), as its economic cycle was not in line with Europe, the Financial Times reported on Wednesday.
Taylor said the foreign exchange rate at which Britain joined monetary union was difficult to forecast -- and could be justified anywhere from 2.20 marks to 2.90 marks.

Britain should not frustrate attempts to form a core euro-zone of Germany, the Benelux countries, Austria and France, he said but added there were dangers inherent in pushing ahead with a broader-based union unless greater convergence emerged.

Taylor said Southern European countries were not ready for monetary union, and allowing Spain and Italy to join 18 months after the planned January 1 1999 start date would not be enough to achieve genuine convergence, the paper quoted him as saying in a lecture in the northern city of Durham.
